plan:
FULL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing executed; all numbers below are protocol constants, documentation facts, or planning estimates — none are results)

D0. QUESTION AND DECISION RULE
Question: does BAdam yield better zero-shot math performance than LoRA when finetuning Llama-3-70B on MathInstruct?
Primary endpoint (researcher decision 2): P = mean of zero-shot accuracy on GSM8K-test (1,319 items) and MATH-test (5,000 items). Per-benchmark accuracies always reported alongside P. If the two benchmarks disagree in direction, that disagreement is reported as a finding; no forced headline verdict. A claim of "BAdam better" requires the BAdam−LoRA difference on P to have a bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero; otherwise the verdict is "no detectable difference."
Hypotheses: H1 = BAdam > LoRA on P; H0 = no detectable difference. Directionally, prior 7B-scale reporting motivates H1, but nothing at 70B is established — that is the gap this experiment addresses.

D1. ARMS
Primary (practitioners' comparison — what the question literally asks):
- A1 BAdam: Llama-3-70B base, full-parameter finetuning with BAdam (bounded-amplitude delta B, levels L, freezing period p as named hyperparameters; D4).
- A2 LoRA: Llama-3-70B base, LoRA r=64, alpha=64, dropout 0.05, applied to all linear projections (q,k,v,o,gate,up,down); optimizer AdamW. Approximate trainable share (~0.1–0.3% of weights) computed from architecture at execution time, not quoted from memory.
- A3 Unfinetuned control: base model, evaluation-only, identical prompts/decoding. No training cost; gives the "did finetuning help at all" baseline.
Sensitivity pair (researcher decision 1, flagged, single sensitivity analysis — a pair because neither method alone answers a comparison): S1 = {BAdam, LoRA} initialized from Llama-3-70B-Instruct, reusing hyperparameters chosen in D3 without re-searching, evaluated on primary endpoints only. The design states explicitly which initialization it assumes and why, so a reader whose intent was Instruct finds the relevant arm rather than a silent assumption.
Secondary budget-matched arms (interpretive layer, feasibility-cuttable — decision 3):
- B1 Scaled LoRA: r=256, all linear modules — raises LoRA's updated-parameter count toward BAdam's.
- B2 Reduced-cycle BAdam: stop at the first incomplete freezing cycle so only a partial parameter fraction has ever received updates.
Feasibility rule (decision 3): if only one budget arm is affordable, drop both extra arms and keep the accuracy-versus-update-budget curves, which require no additional training because the budget axes are measured from all completed runs (D5).

D2. DATA AND CONTAMINATION (researcher decision 4 — strict)
Corpus: MathInstruct (~394K instruction–solution pairs) as released, with three fixed exclusions.
(a) Held-out selection slice: 2,000 MathInstruct samples (fixed seed) removed from training, used ONLY for hyperparameter/LR selection via assistant-token NLL. Benchmark test sets are never used for training or selection — stated as a hard invariant.
(b) Near-duplicate screen vs GSM8K-test and MATH-test: normalized exact match plus token-shingle Jaccard and MinHash-LSH above pre-registered thresholds, including numeric-abstraction comparison (digit-masked text) because math near-duplicates often differ only in numbers. Flagged items are excluded from training.
(c) Stratified reporting: every headline result is additionally reported split by whether each test item had a raw-corpus near-duplicate (exposed vs clean strata). Sensitivity run (feasibility-cuttable): one uncleaned-corpus training run of the cheaper LoRA arm; because the quantity of interest is the BAdam−LoRA difference, a single run estimates whether leakage shifts the gap, and it is the cheaper arm so the leak-audit costs less.
Preprocessing: chat-style templating, loss on assistant tokens only, max length 4,096 with truncation rate reported; no curriculum filtering (assumption); 1 epoch per training run.

D3. OPTIMIZER SELECTION — PRE-REGISTERED, SHARED BUDGET (researcher decision 5)
The BAdam paper did not establish B, L, p, or usable LR at 70B; these are named hyperparameters, not quoted values.
- Search budget: ≤4 configs per method for LR on A1/A2; for BAdam, B and p each varied over 2 values at the median grid LR (≤2 additional configs). Each search run: 1 pass over 20% of the cleaned corpus; selection = lowest assistant-token NLL on the D2(a) slice. Chosen values are recorded as protocol outputs.
- LR grids (protocol constants): LoRA {5e-5, 1e-4, 2e-4, 4e-4}; BAdam {2e-5, 1e-4, 5e-4, 2e-3}. Ranges to be sanity-anchored to the source paper's reported 7B-scale ranges at execution. Pre-registered boundary rule: if the best config is at the top grid point, extend the grid once upward (counts against budget) — prevents "one optimizer was untuned" artifacts.
- BAdam defaults to verify against the reference implementation before fixing grid centers: B≈1e-3, L≈10, p≈100 (paper defaults at smaller scale; labeled memory-to-verify, not authority). Grid: B {1e-3, 1e-2}, p {100, 250}.
- LoRA hyperparameters other than LR are fixed at the practitioner settings above (primary comparison means each method at its recommended configuration, not jointly tuned to exhaustion — symmetric treatment).
- All other training constants identical across arms: AdamW betas/eps defaults, cosine schedule to zero after warmup (3%), bf16, global batch fixed in tokens across arms, same data order and epoch count.

D4. EVALUATION (zero-shot = zero in-context exemplars; assumption labeled)
Benchmarks: primary GSM8K-test and MATH-test; secondary out-of-domain zero-shot transfer: SVAMP, AsDiv, TabMWP, AQuA (AQuA scored as multiple-choice accuracy); MATH additionally stratified by difficulty level 1–5.
Protocol constants identical across all arms and checkpoints: one fixed prompt template per benchmark; greedy decoding (temperature 0); max_new_tokens 1,024 (GSM8K) / 2,048 (MATH); scoring via standard extractors — GSM8K numeric final-answer match, MATH \boxed{} symbolic equivalence (sympy checker). Report per-arm unextractable/format-failure rate; a correctness metric conditioned on successful extraction is reported alongside the naive one, so a "win" cannot silently be a format-compliance win.
Checkpoints: final checkpoint is primary; a fixed mid-training evaluation point is logged for the training-dynamics record (not endpoint-bearing).

D5. ANALYSIS PLAN
1. Primary: P and per-benchmark accuracies per arm; bootstrap 95% CIs resampling test items (stratified by benchmark); item-level paired (McNemar-style) win/loss/tie between A1 and A2, which remains informative with a single seed.
2. Interpretive layer: accuracy plotted against two measured budget axes — (i) fraction of parameters receiving nonzero updates per step (accounting for BAdam's block schedule and LoRA's fixed mask), and (ii) cumulative optimizer-step FLOPs and tokens seen. Every run logs these; curves are populated by primary arms even if budget arms are cut.
3. Contamination stratified analysis (D2c) on all primary results.
4. Variance: target 3 seeds per primary arm (assumption/aspiration); with 1 seed, explicitly state that item bootstraps capture evaluation variance only, not run-to-run training variance.
5. Secondary OOD sets reported as a transfer table; they cannot override the primary endpoint.

D6. FEASIBILITY (explicit)
Planning estimates (order-of-magnitude, not results): bf16 weights ≈ 140 GB. LoRA-70B fits one 8×80 GB node (FSDP/ZeRO-3 + activation checkpointing; tiny optimizer state). Full-parameter BAdam-70B needs ~1–2 such nodes; its memory advantage over vanilla AdamW is that fp32 moments exist only for the active block. One 1-epoch run over ~0.4–0.7B documented corpus tokens at ~6·N·D FLOPs and a 25–35% MFU assumption gives roughly 10^3 GPU-hours per training run; with LR search (≈6 short runs at 20% data) and 3 seeds, the full protocol is plausibly 2–4×10^4 GPU-hours — i.e., multi-node, multi-week. This environment (224 CPUs, no GPU, no network) executes none of it.
Pre-registered cut order under pressure: (1) B1/B2 budget arms (curves survive from logged budget statistics); (2) uncleaned-corpus leak sensitivity run; (3) Instruct-init sensitivity pair; (4) seeds 3→2→1; (5) OOD secondary sets (drop AQuA, TabMWP first); LR grid narrows before seeds never go below 1; A3 control is evaluation-only and is never cut.
If only the primary comparison is affordable, the design still delivers: practitioners' A1-vs-A2-vs-A3 with symmetric LR selection, cleaned data, primary endpoint with CIs, item-level paired tests, and measured update-budget statistics — losing only the extra trained points on the budget axes, the initialization and leakage sensitivity checks, and training-variance estimation.

D7. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY OR WEAKEN THE CONCLUSION
A BAdam win is falsified or discounted if: (i) LoRA's LR curve is still rising at its grid top or BAdam's best sits at its boundary — an optimizer-tuning artifact (mitigated by the symmetric grid and boundary rule, but detectable by reporting full LR curves); (ii) the win concentrates entirely in the contamination-exposed stratum; (iii) the win vanishes once unextractable-format outputs are handled, i.e., it is format compliance rather than math correctness; (iv) with multiple seeds the seed spread swallows the gap; (v) GSM8K and MATH disagree in direction — reported, not averaged away silently (the averaged endpoint decides the formal claim, the disaggregation reports the caveat); (vi) the OOD transfer table reverses the ranking, suggesting benchmark-specific overfitting. A BAdam loss equally falsifies H1 and is reported with the same disaggregations.

CONSTRAINTS HONORED: no experiment was run; no numbers above are results (they are protocol constants, documentation facts, or labeled planning estimates); assumptions are labeled here and in the assumptions list; researcher decisions 1–5 are marked as decisions, not source facts.
